item.title: #3626105: Release runtime theme registries after destruction
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +26/−1 · php +26/−1
  • Diff: 96cfe41
  • Discussion: #3626105 · 4 contributors · 11 comments
  • Followers: 7
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 4 contributors

Summary

On persistent PHP workers such as FrankenPHP in worker mode, the theme registry service can outlive a request. After the first request's cleanup, later requests could log "Theme hook %hook not found." and render nothing for the affected hooks. The registry now discards its runtime collectors during cleanup, so the next request gets fresh ones and theme hooks are found again. Sites on classic PHP-FPM or Apache are not affected.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Registry::destruct() called destruct() on each collector in $this->runtimeRegistry but kept them. CacheCollector::destruct() persists pending changes and resets storage. Registry::getRuntime() then returned the same retained, emptied ThemeRegistry, whose has() and get() read that storage directly. So previously registered hooks came back as missing, and ThemeManager::render() logged the "not found" message and returned FALSE.

The fix copies $this->runtimeRegistry to a local variable, sets the property to [], then destructs the copies. The next getRuntime() call builds a new ThemeRegistry, whose constructor loads the runtime cache or initializes on a miss. Repeated destruct() calls also skip collectors that were already processed. A new kernel test, testRuntimeRegistryAfterDestruct() in RegistryTest, checks that a hook is still found after destruct() and that a different collector instance is returned. The committer noted that for persistent workers it may be better not to clean up these collectors at all, so a loaded registry stays available across requests. That is left for later work.

  • Committed: October 5, 2026 (9 days later)

item.title: #3568767: Deprecate Media::getRequestTime()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +12/−9 · php +12/−9
  • Discussion: #3568767 · 5 contributors · 28 comments
  • Followers: 6
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

The Media entity's getRequestTime() method, previously undocumented beyond a generic {@inheritdoc} comment despite not actually overriding anything, is now deprecated with no replacement. The method will be removed in Drupal 13. It is no longer used internally by Drupal core, so most sites are unaffected; only code that explicitly calls Media::getRequestTime() needs to change.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Media::getRequestTime() is deprecated in drupal:12.1.0 and removed from drupal:13.0.0, with no replacement.

Technical details

The created base field on the Media entity used Media::getRequestTime() as its setDefaultValueCallback(), even though the method simply returned \Drupal::time()->getRequestTime(), the same value the created field type (CreatedItem::applyDefaultValue()) already sets by default. Since the callback was redundant, it was removed from Media::baseFieldDefinitions() entirely rather than just documented, and the method itself was marked @deprecated with a proper docblock, a return type hint (: int), and a trigger_error() call pointing to the change record at https://www.drupal.org/node/3624921. The corresponding PHPStan baseline entry for the method's missing return type was also removed since the new return type hint makes it unnecessary.

Upgrade

Replace any direct calls to the deprecated method:

// Before:
$time = Media::getRequestTime();

// After:
$time = \Drupal::time()->getRequestTime();

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: January 21, 2026

Key contributors

  • avpaderno
  • dcam
  • catch (Third and Grove)

Collaboration

What started as a documentation-only fix changed direction after catch pointed out that getRequestTime() wasn't needed at all, since CreatedItem already defaults the created field to the request time without it; this prompted removing the setDefaultValueCallback() usage and deprecating the method instead of just documenting it. Later, catch also caught that the deprecation's target version needed updating once Drupal 12.0.x opened, which avpaderno corrected to drupal:12.1.0 after initially targeting the wrong release.

item.title: #3081025: Remove technical debt and complication from when doTrustedCallback() could either trigger errors or throw exceptions
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +57/−44 · php +57/−44
  • Diff: de58972
  • Discussion: #3081025 · 9 contributors · 39 comments
  • Followers: 14
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 9 contributors

Summary

When Drupal detects an "untrusted" callback (for example in a render array), it now always throws an exception rather than offering an option to only log a silenced deprecation warning instead. This closes a long-standing loophole left over from the original security hardening work in #2966327: Drupal core itself has thrown the exception unconditionally since Drupal 9, but the old $error_type escape hatch was still present in the API for anyone who wanted to opt into the softer, warning-only behavior. That option is now deprecated and will disappear in Drupal 13.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: TrustedCallbackInterface::THROW_EXCEPTION and TrustedCallbackInterface::TRIGGER_SILENCED_DEPRECATION are deprecated, and the $error_type parameter of DoTrustedCallbackTrait::doTrustedCallback() / StaticTrustedCallbackHelper::callback() is removed from the method signature; passing a 5th argument now triggers a deprecation notice and is removed in Drupal 13.0.0.

Technical details

DoTrustedCallbackTrait::doTrustedCallback() and StaticTrustedCallbackHelper::callback() dropped the $error_type parameter from their signatures; the method body no longer branches on TRIGGER_SILENCED_DEPRECATION and simply throws Drupal\Core\Security\UntrustedCallbackException whenever a callback fails the trusted-callback check. Renderer::doCallback() was updated accordingly to call doTrustedCallback() without an error-type argument.

Because $extra_trusted_interface was the 5th parameter and $error_type the 4th, removing $error_type from the signature would silently break any caller still passing both. To preserve backward compatibility, both methods now use func_num_args()/func_get_arg(4): if a 5th argument is still supplied, it is treated as the (now 4th-position) $extra_trusted_interface value and a deprecation notice is triggered rather than a hard fatal. The two now-unused TrustedCallbackInterface constants (THROW_EXCEPTION, TRIGGER_SILENCED_DEPRECATION) are marked @deprecated in their docblocks rather than removed outright, consistent with the Drupal core deprecation policy.

Upgrade

Remove any explicit $error_type argument (TrustedCallbackInterface::THROW_EXCEPTION or TrustedCallbackInterface::TRIGGER_SILENCED_DEPRECATION) from calls to doTrustedCallback() or StaticTrustedCallbackHelper::callback(). If you need to pass $extra_trusted_interface, it is now the 4th argument:

// Before:
$this->doTrustedCallback($callback, $args, $message, TrustedCallbackInterface::THROW_EXCEPTION, RenderCallbackInterface::class);

// After:
$this->doTrustedCallback($callback, $args, $message, RenderCallbackInterface::class);

Untrusted callbacks always throw Drupal\Core\Security\UntrustedCallbackException now; there is no replacement for the silenced-deprecation behavior.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: September 12, 2019
  • Committed: October 1, 2026 (7 years later)

Key contributors

  • xjm
  • dww
  • berdir
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • samuel.mortenson
  • larowlan (PreviousNext)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

This issue sat postponed for years: in 2020 alexpott argued it shouldn't proceed until #2966711 (trusted callbacks for form arrays) was settled, "possibly never", since contrib might still want the deprecation path for its own callback types. dww and berdir independently reached the same conclusion after digging into core/lib/Drupal/Core/Security/DoTrustedCallbackTrait.php and discovering that Drupal 9's Renderer.php was already unconditionally throwing exceptions, so the issue was really about removing now-dead plumbing rather than closing a live security gap. When larowlan revived the issue in 2025 ahead of Drupal 12, alexpott used a code search across contrib (turning up a real caller in twig_field_value) to confirm that simply deleting the $error_type parameter would break existing code, and added the func_num_args()-based deprecation shim so those callers get a warning instead of a fatal error.

item.title: #3585957: Prevent the navigation sidebar being rendered via big pipe
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.4.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +22/−17 · yml +17/−17 · php +5
  • Diff: 9afec8f
  • Discussion: #3585957 · 6 contributors · 32 comments
  • Followers: 13
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 6 contributors

Summary

When the new navigation sidebar's render cache was cold, Drupal used BigPipe to stream it in after the rest of the page had already loaded. This caused the whole page content to visibly jump sideways as the sidebar popped in, an effect known as content layout shift (jank). This fix stops the navigation sidebar from being deferred via BigPipe, so it renders inline with the rest of the page instead. This can make the initial page response marginally slower on a cache miss, but avoids the jarring layout shift, and testing also showed it slightly reduces the number of separate asset/cache operations needed for the page.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The fix adds #placeholder_strategy_denylist to the navigation render element built in NavigationRenderer::buildNavigation() (core/modules/navigation/src/NavigationRenderer.php), denylisting BigPipeStrategy::class. This is the same mechanism already used elsewhere in core, such as BlockViewBuilder and Core\Render\Element\StatusMessages, to opt a #lazy_builder placeholder out of BigPipe handling via ChainedPlaceholderStrategy. The element still has #create_placeholder set, so it keeps its own cache item and placeholder behavior, it simply is no longer eligible to be swapped in asynchronously by BigPipe; it now renders synchronously with the rest of the page.

A @todo comment ties this to #3505610, a stalled attempt to instead add a proper placeholder preview (skeleton) for the navigation sidebar; once that lands, this denylisting is intended to be removed. During review, a tester found that on HEAD the BigPipe-rendered navigation could fail entirely with a big_pipe.commands.js JS error on first cache clear, a symptom suspected to be related to a race condition discussed in #3566843; this change avoids that failure mode as well since the sidebar no longer goes through BigPipe's swap mechanism. Performance test baselines (StylesheetCount, QueryCount, CacheGetCount, CacheSetCount) were updated to reflect the slightly different asset/cache call counts caused by loading navigation CSS/JS with the main request instead of as a separate BigPipe response.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: April 21, 2026
  • Committed: September 8, 2026 (4 months later)

Key contributors

  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • godotislate

Collaboration

The committer, godotislate, found while testing the MR on Umami that the navigation sidebar could fail to render at all on HEAD with a console TypeError from big_pipe.commands.js, and linked it to a race condition catch (berdir) had described in #3566843. catch, the issue author, noted the change actually produced a small performance test improvement because navigation assets load with the main request instead of a separate BigPipe round trip.

item.title: #3516706: Disallow dangerous filenames e.g. command injection characters
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +76/−3 · php +76/−3
  • Diff: c30d609
  • Discussion: #3516706 · 13 contributors · 96 comments
  • Followers: 24
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 13 contributors

Summary

Drupal now automatically strips a fixed set of dangerous characters, including shell metacharacters like ` $ ; | & `, quotes, angle brackets, control characters, and path separators, from the names of newly uploaded files, replacing them with underscores. This closes off a potential command-injection or XSS vector that could arise if a filename containing such characters was later passed unsafely to a shell command or rendered without escaping. The change applies to every site automatically and cannot be turned off; only newly uploaded files are affected, existing filenames are left untouched. Filenames that would otherwise collapse to nothing (e.g. ... or files with only unsafe characters before the extension) now fall back to unnamed instead of becoming empty, and a leading dash or dot left after sanitization is also handled so the result can't be mistaken for a command-line option or a hidden dotfile. Whitespace in filenames is unaffected, that remains governed by the existing optional filename_sanitization setting.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The logic lives in \Drupal\file\EventSubscriber\SecurityFileUploadEventSubscriber::sanitizeName(), which already ran last in the FileUploadSanitizeNameEvent chain and already stripped null bytes unconditionally, so the new mandatory stripping was added there rather than in the configurable FileEventSubscriber. A new INSECURE_CHARACTERS PCRE constant (built with Unicode property classes \p{Cc} for control characters and \p{Cf} for invisible format/bidi-override characters, plus a literal set of shell metacharacters, quotes, path separators, # and %) is matched and replaced with _ via preg_replace(). After that substitution, a leading - is trimmed (since many CLI tools parse a leading dash as an option), and if the result is empty or starts with . it is prefixed with the FALLBACK_FILENAME constant unnamed, relying on the existing suffixing in FileSystem::createFilename() to disambiguate collisions (unnamed_0, unnamed_1, etc).

The issue went through several design iterations, an earlier approach tried to also default-enable whitespace replacement and made the character list configurable via file.settings, but both were dropped: whitespace substitution was judged too disruptive to ship as a default and was left as the existing opt-in setting, and making the blocked-character list configurable was rejected because a misconfigured list could reintroduce the vulnerability. Characters are now replaced rather than deleted outright, a change from an earlier iteration, so that e.g. Love&War.pdf becomes Love_War.pdf rather than LoveWar.pdf, preserving more of the original separation between words. A related follow-up, #3562543, fixed a crash in the whitespace-replacement regex when fed invalid UTF-8 and landed first as a prerequisite.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: April 1, 2025
  • Committed: September 19, 2026 (1 year later)

Key contributors

  • mcdruid (Acquia)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • cmlara (DM13 Security LLC)
  • kim.pepper (PreviousNext)
  • benjifisher (Harvard Web Publishing)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • mohit_aghera (PreviousNext)
  • larowlan (PreviousNext)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • xjm (xjm)

Collaboration

The issue spent over a year iterating on scope. mcdruid (the reporter) and kim.pepper went back and forth on whether to strip a fixed list of "dangerous" characters versus making the list configurable, and whether to default-enable whitespace replacement; a usability team review (summarized by mcdruid in comment #26 and confirmed by benjifisher in #30) concluded that stripping punctuation should be non-negotiable but replacing whitespace should remain an opt-in default. Attempting to flip the whitespace default uncovered an unrelated bug (a preg_replace() call returning null on malformed UTF-8 input), which kim.pepper and mcdruid debugged together and split off into the prerequisite issue #3562543. After that landed, mcdruid disclosed using Claude to help work out the final implementation pushed to the MR, abandoning the configurable, whitespace-replacing approach in favor of a simpler, non-configurable, replace-not-remove scheme. cmlara then pushed back strongly on making the protection non-configurable and on stripping characters that appear in legitimate filenames, arguing it could create a false sense of safety in downstream code and cause reputational issues if parts of filenames like Love&War.pdf were silently dropped. That critique led alexpott and mcdruid to change the implementation from removing characters to replacing them with _, and longwave and xjm weighed in to support keeping the list non-configurable, reasoning that configurability of a security control increases risk of misconfiguration for comparatively little benefit. larowlan, reviewing the final regex character by character with regex101, committed the change and it was backported to 11.5.x by xjm shortly before the beta1 tag.

item.title: #3466088: [meta] Deprecate dependencies, libraries, modules, and themes that will be removed from Drupal 12 core
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical plan
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3466088 · 6 contributors · 44 comments
  • Followers: 30
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 6 contributors

Summary

This is the master tracking (meta) issue that coordinated Drupal's plan to slim down core ahead of Drupal 12 by removing a batch of modules and themes and moving them to standalone contributed projects instead. Over roughly a year and a half of follow-up, the Ban, Contact, Field Layout, History, Migrate Drupal, Migrate Drupal UI, Search, Settings Tray, Shortcut, and Telephone modules, the Toolbar module, and the Claro, Stable 9, and Olivero themes were all deprecated and had contrib equivalents prepared. Site owners using any of these should start evaluating and installing the contributed replacement before updating to Drupal 12, since the core versions will no longer be available. The underlying code changes (deprecation notices, test coverage moved, contrib packages created) were done in each linked child meta issue rather than in this one.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Ban, Contact, Field Layout, History, Migrate Drupal, Migrate Drupal UI, Search, Settings Tray, Shortcut, Telephone, and Toolbar modules, plus the Claro, Stable 9, and Olivero themes, are deprecated in Drupal 11.x and planned for removal in Drupal 12, with equivalent contributed projects taking their place.

Technical details

No code changed directly in this issue; it is a coordination hub whose body and comments were kept updated as each module/theme reached deprecation (and in most cases full removal) in core, with checkmarks added as each linked meta issue closed. Each deprecated module or theme follows the same pattern: core marks the extension deprecated in *.info.yml/code with @deprecated notices, a contributed project is created at drupal.org as the ongoing maintenance home, and once the contrib package is stable the module or theme is removed from core in a later release (several, like Field Layout, Toolbar, and Olivero, were fully removed from core rather than merely deprecated by the time this meta issue closed). Related infrastructure work also tracked here includes dropping jQuery UI dependencies (#3076171, #2158943), replacing the Archive_Tar library usage (#3556706), and generating new database fixtures without the deprecated modules for update-path tests (#3569127). See the individual meta issues, including #3482198 (Ban), #3520460 (Contact), #3517712 (Field Layout), and #3315257 (Migrate Drupal/Migrate Drupal UI), for the actual code and API details of each deprecation.

Contribution

quietone maintained this meta issue for roughly a year and a half, posting regular status updates as each child deprecation issue progressed and finally closing it after Toolbar, the last item, was completed. catch pushed to keep the effort moving, noting that deprecating these modules has to happen well before Drupal 12.0.0 given the multiple steps involved. item.title: #2265487: ConfigEntity based lists with items containing non-ascii characters are not sorted correctly
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 11 files, +165/−9 · php +158/−8 · lock +4/−1 · json +3
  • Diff: 8cd44d4
  • Discussion: #2265487 · 16 contributors · 171 comments
  • Followers: 19

Summary

Lists built from configuration entities, such as content type lists, vocabularies, view modes, blocks, and date formats, are now sorted correctly when their labels contain accented or non-ASCII characters (like é, ñ). Previously these items were pushed to the end of alphabetically sorted lists regardless of their actual letter, because the sort relied on a plain byte comparison. As a side effect, embedded numbers now sort numerically too (for example "Format 10x10" before "Format 100x100"), and block labels, which were previously sorted case-sensitively, are now sorted case-insensitively like other config entities.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New Drupal\Core\Utility\NaturalSort::strnatcasecmp() static method, a locale-aware, collation-based drop-in replacement for PHP's strnatcasecmp(), used internally by config entity sort methods.

Technical details

The various ::sort() implementations across config entity classes (ConfigEntityBase, DateFormat, EntityDisplayModeBase, Language, Block, Action) called PHP's byte-wise strnatcasecmp() (or, in Block's case, strcmp()) to order labels, which is locale-unaware and sorts accented characters after all plain ASCII letters. The fix adds a new final class Drupal\Core\Utility\NaturalSort with a static strnatcasecmp(string $string1, string $string2, ?string $langcode = NULL) method that, when the intl extension is loaded, builds (and caches per langcode in a static array) a \Collator for the given or current language and enables Collator::NUMERIC_COLLATION so embedded numbers compare numerically. It falls back to plain strnatcasecmp() when intl isn't available or no langcode can be resolved. All the affected ::sort() methods were updated to call this helper instead of the raw PHP functions.

Getting there took several redesigns. An earlier iteration deprecated ConfigEntityBase::sort() in favor of new sortEntities()/compare() methods and added a symfony/polyfill-intl-icu dependency as a fallback when intl is missing; that version was committed to 11.x, then reverted within hours because Symfony\Polyfill\Intl\Icu\Collator::compare() wasn't actually implemented, which crashed drush cr and any other code path on sites without the intl extension (duplicate issue #3516545). The version that eventually landed drops the polyfill dependency entirely and keeps the original sort() method signatures unchanged, so there is no deprecation and no new required dependency: composer.json only gained a suggest entry for ext-intl.

A follow-up issue, #3624817, tracks adding a NaturalSort::natcasesort() helper and converting other locale-sensitive strnatcasecmp()/strcmp() call sites across core (e.g. SortArray, plugin collection sort helpers) to use this new utility.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">Code that needs locale-aware label sorting can use the new helper instead of PHP's native function:

use Drupal\Core\Utility\NaturalSort;

usort($items, fn($a, $b) => NaturalSort::strnatcasecmp($a->label(), $b->label()));

Install the PHP intl extension (now suggested in composer.json) to get locale-aware collation; without it the method transparently falls back to strnatcasecmp().</upgrade> <parameter name="collaboration">This bug report sat open for nearly a decade and went through several design iterations before landing. longwave raised a performance concern about invoking services inside the sort callback and questioned whether transliteration was the right approach, which led sleitner to switch the implementation to PHP's Collator (comments around #31). After catch committed an iteration that deprecated sort() and added a Symfony polyfill dependency, acbramley discovered it caused a fatal error ("Class Collator not found") on sites without the intl extension because the polyfill's Collator::compare() wasn't implemented; catch reverted the commit the same day and reopened the issue to fix it properly (duplicate #3516545). alexpott then did an extensive review, identified that Collator needed NUMERIC_COLLATION enabled to beat plain strnatcasecmp() even for English sites, and proposed abandoning the sort()/sortEntities() API split in favor of the simpler, purely additive NaturalSort utility class that ultimately shipped, crediting sleitner for "an amazing job of keeping up with all my reviews" across the many reroll and rebase cycles (smustgrave similarly thanked sleitner for "keeping up with all the rebases").</collaboration> <parameter name="ai_disclosures">[]

item.title: #3626470: Review Drupal 12 and 11.x composer dependencies for allowed versions with CVEs
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +8/−8 · json +5/−5 · lock +3/−3
  • Diff: d29add7
  • Discussion: #3626470 · 3 contributors · 18 comments
  • Followers: 4
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 3 contributors

Summary

Drupal's composer.json files (root and core/) had their minimum allowed dependency versions raised so that even the lowest versions Composer is willing to resolve are not affected by known CVEs. The runtime dependency guzzlehttp/guzzle now requires at least 8.0.1, and the development-only dependencies composer/composer and phpunit/phpunit had their floors raised too. This is a hardening change with no behavioral effect on a normal composer update: sites that already install recent versions of these libraries are unaffected, but the change closes a gap where composer update --prefer-lowest or a minimal fresh install could previously land on a vulnerable version.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: Minimum allowed guzzlehttp/guzzle version raised from ^8.0 to ^8.0.1 in core's runtime requirements; dev-only minimums for composer/composer (^2.8.1 to ^2.10.3) and phpunit/phpunit (^12.5.15 to ^12.5.22) were also raised.

Technical details

The issue was triggered by running composer audit --locked combined with composer update --prefer-lowest (with COMPOSER_NO_SECURITY_BLOCKING=1 to bypass Composer's own blocking) to see which CVEs would affect the lowest versions Drupal's constraints technically allow, as opposed to the versions actually pinned in composer.lock. That audit found advisories affecting composer/composer, google/protobuf, guzzlehttp/guzzle, guzzlehttp/psr7, squizlabs/php_codesniffer, and symfony/polyfill-intl-idn at their lowest allowed versions.

Summary

Recipes that configure a CKEditor 5 toolbar can now add several buttons in a single step. Previously the addItemToToolbar config action only accepted one toolbar item at a time, so a recipe that needed to add several buttons had to repeat the action once per button. The new addItemsToToolbar action accepts a list of items, each either a button name or an options array (for example to set position or allow_duplicate), and applies them all in one pass.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New hook_config_action_alter() lets modules alter or alias config action plugin definitions, and a new editor:addItemsToToolbar config action adds multiple CKEditor 5 toolbar items in a single recipe action.

Technical details

Drupal\ckeditor5\Plugin\ConfigAction\AddItemToToolbar::apply() now normalizes its $value argument: a plain string or an associative array is treated as a single item and wrapped in a list, while an indexed array is treated as multiple items. Each item is delegated to a new private applySingle() method, which contains the original per-item logic (position, replace, allow_duplicate, plugin default configuration), and the editor entity is saved only once at the end if anything actually changed. Invalid input, an empty list, a non-string/array item, or an item missing item_name, now throws a ConfigActionException with a descriptive message instead of failing a silent assert().

Because the #[ConfigAction] attribute isn't repeatable, the plural addItemsToToolbar isn't a second plugin class: it's registered as an alias of editor:addItemToToolbar inside Ckeditor5Hooks::configActionAlter(), which implements the new hook_config_action_alter() documented in core.api.php. Maintainers noted in review that using an alter hook for aliasing is a stopgap that decouples the plural action from its singular definition, and that dedicated alias support on the ConfigAction attribute would be a cleaner long term solution, left as a followup.

To add multiple CKEditor 5 toolbar buttons in a recipe, replace repeated addItemToToolbar calls with a single addItemsToToolbar call taking a list:

  actions:
    editor.editor.content_format:
      addItemsToToolbar:
        - specialCharacters
        - codeBlock
        -
          item_name: italic
          position: 0
          allow_duplicate: true

Summary

Continuing the work started in #3411490, the hook_schema() implementations of core's regular (non-test) modules, comment, dblog, file, layout_builder, node, user, and workspaces, have been converted from the traditional nested associative array format to the newer object-oriented SchemaDefinition API. Modules that still return the legacy array format keep working, but now trigger a deprecation notice, since Drupal 13 will require the object-based format. While doing this conversion, the team discovered that dblog's watchdog.wid column was not actually unsigned as its own documentation claimed; an update function now corrects existing sites' schema to match.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: dblog_update_12100() deletes any rows with a negative wid and converts the watchdog.wid primary key column to an unsigned big integer, matching the schema as actually declared.
  • Deprecation: Returning a legacy array from hook_schema() (rather than a Drupal\Core\Database\SchemaDefinition\Schema object) to ModuleInstaller::installSchema()/uninstallSchema() or to SchemaInspector::getTablesSpecification() is deprecated in drupal:12.1.0 and will be removed in drupal:13.0.0.

Technical details

The converted hook_schema() implementations now build a Schema object out of Table, Column, Index, PrimaryKey, and ForeignKey value objects (e.g. Column::varcharAscii(name: 'entity_type', length: EntityTypeInterface::ID_MAX_LENGTH, ...)) instead of returning nested PHP arrays. Validation was tightened on the SchemaDefinition value objects themselves: Column::validate() now throws a SchemaDefinitionException if length is missing for Varchar/VarcharAscii columns, Schema::validate() rejects duplicate table names, and Table::validate() (via a new columnNames() method) rejects duplicate column names within a table.

The conversion surfaced a real discrepancy: dblog_schema()'s watchdog.wid was declared unsigned: TRUE under the new definition, but the live database column was not actually enforced as unsigned. dblog_update_12100() removes any rows with negative wid values and runs changeField() to make the column unsigned, with a new UpdatePathTest exercising the negative-id-then-update scenario. Conversion of schemata defined by test modules was explicitly postponed to a follow-up issue, per review feedback from amateescu, to keep this change reviewable.

Module maintainers should convert their hook_schema() implementations from arrays to SchemaDefinition objects to avoid deprecation notices, for example:

function mymodule_schema(): Schema {
  $tables[] = new Table(
    name: 'mymodule_table',
    description: '...',
    columns: [
      Column::int(
        name: 'id',
        description: '...',
        unsigned: TRUE,
        notNull: TRUE,
        default: new IntValue(0),
      ),
    ],
    primaryKey: new PrimaryKey(['id']),
  );

  return new Schema(
    type: SchemaDefinitionType::Module,
    name: 'mymodule',
    tables: $tables,
  );
}

Summary

Twig 3.30 changed how its escape/e filter compiles, and Drupal's mechanism for swapping in its own MarkupInterface-aware escaping broke as a result: every templated page threw a TypeError and produced a white screen of death. This fix restores compatibility so sites can run Drupal with Twig 3.30 (or Twig 3.28/3.29) without the crash. Anyone who had pinned twig/twig to an older version as a workaround can lift that pin once they update to a core release containing this fix.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Twig 3.30 introduced a dedicated EscapeFilter node that compiles directly to $this->escaper->escape(...). Drupal's TwigNodeVisitor::leaveNode() previously handled escape/e filters by swapping the compiled node's callable to Drupal's own drupal_escape filter, but leaving Twig's own EscapeFilter node in place to build the call. Twig 3.30 still emitted the direct escaper->escape() call, but built its arguments for drupal_escape (which needs the environment as its first parameter), so $this->env was inserted as an extra leading argument, every other argument shifted over, and null (the charset) ended up in the $autoescape boolean slot.

Because Twig loads Drupal's extension after its own EscaperExtension, and later-registered filters of the same name win, Twig's built-in escape node/filter is overridden outright and never compiled, so the argument-shifting bug can't occur regardless of Twig version. A new TwigExtension::escapeFilterIsSafe() static method replaces the previous reliance on Twig's internal twig_escape_filter_is_safe helper as the is_safe_callback. TwigNodeVisitor::leaveNode() was simplified accordingly: it no longer swaps the node's callable, it just checks whether the filter name is escape, e, or drupal_escape to set $this->skipRenderVarFunction. item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core

Summary

Required entity reference fields using the "Select list" widget (for example a required taxonomy term reference) could silently corrupt data. If the referenced entity was deleted, or became inaccessible to the current user, the widget's usual "- Select a value -" placeholder disappeared and the select box defaulted to the first available option instead. Editors who saved the form without noticing would overwrite the field with an unintended value. Now, when a required single-value select has no valid selection, the widget adds a "- Select a value -" option and forces the editor to explicitly pick a real value before the form can be saved, rather than defaulting to an arbitrary option.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The bug was in OptionsSelectWidget::getEmptyLabel(), which decided whether to show a placeholder option based solely on $this->has_value (whether the field item list originally had a value), not on whether that value was still present among the currently available options. When a referenced entity was deleted or became inaccessible, has_value remained TRUE even though the resulting default value was empty, so no placeholder was added and the browser's <select> fell back to auto-selecting its first <option>.

The fix moves the decision into OptionsSelectWidget::formElement(): it computes $options and $selected directly, determines whether the field will render as a multiple select (accounting for the case where a multi-value field collapses to a single select because only one option remains), and if the field is required, not multiple, and $selected is empty, prepends a synthetic _none option labeled "- Select a value -" so the browser has an explicit non-answer to fall back to instead of the first real option. getEmptyLabel() itself is simplified to only return '- None -' for non-required fields (used elsewhere for the optional case) and no longer inspects has_value at all.

item.title: #3037054: Deprecate drupal_static_reset() and drupal_static()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev

Summary

The long-standing procedural helpers drupal_static() and drupal_static_reset(), used to define reset-able static variables inside functions, are now formally deprecated and will be removed in Drupal 13.0.0. Sites and modules that still call these functions directly will start seeing deprecation notices and should switch to the memory cache backend instead. Core's own remaining internal callers (in batch processing, CSS optimization, machine name form validation, comment search indexing, and admin theme settings overrides) have already been converted to use \Drupal::cache('memory') directly.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: drupal_static() and drupal_static_reset() are deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and removed in drupal:13.0.0; use \Drupal::cache('memory')->get(), ->set(), and ->delete() instead.

Technical details

The deprecation notices are added directly inside drupal_static() and drupal_static_reset() in core/includes/bootstrap.inc. Because both functions can legitimately be called many times per request (and core itself still needs to call drupal_static_reset() globally to flush all statics in a few places), a naive @trigger_error() on every call would spam PHPUnit's deprecation handling and logs. To avoid that, each function first checks a per-$name marker in \Drupal::cache('memory'); the deprecation is triggered only the first time a given $name is seen in the request, then the marker cache entry suppresses further triggers for that name.

A special sentinel value, 'clear_all_skip_deprecation', was introduced so that core's own "reset every static" call sites (drupal_flush_all_caches(), KernelTestBase::tearDown(), and FunctionalTestSetupTrait::tearDown()) can still clear all statics via drupal_static_reset() without triggering the deprecation on themselves; these call sites are marked with // @phpstan-ignore function.deprecated.

Remaining core call sites that used drupal_static() as a lightweight per-request cache (_batch_needs_update() in core/includes/batch.inc, FormElementBase/MachineName::getTransliterationLanguageOverrides(), CommentHooks::nodeUpdateIndex(), and Settings::userOverrideEnabled() in core/themes/default_admin) were rewritten to read and write \Drupal::cache('memory') directly, matching the pattern already used elsewhere for drupal_static_reset() replacements like options.allowed_values. ResettableStaticTest was updated with #[IgnoreDeprecations] and expectUserDeprecationMessage() assertions to cover the new deprecation paths.

Upgrade

Replace direct calls to drupal_static() and drupal_static_reset() with the memory cache backend. For example, code that previously did:

$overrides = &drupal_static(__CLASS__ . '_' . __METHOD__, []);

should become:

$cid = __CLASS__ . '_' . __METHOD__;
$cached = \Drupal::cache('memory')->get($cid);
$overrides = $cached->data ?? [];
// ... after computing/updating $overrides:
\Drupal::cache('memory')->set($cid, $overrides);

And a reset call like:

drupal_static_reset('my_cache_id');

becomes:

\Drupal::cache('memory')->delete('my_cache_id');

Calling drupal_static_reset() with no arguments (to reset all statics) is also deprecated; there is no direct drop-in replacement for clearing every memory cache entry at once, so only internal core bootstrap code retains this ability via the 'clear_all_skip_deprecation' sentinel.

  • Opened: March 2, 2019
  • Committed: September 24, 2026 (7 years later)

item.description:

Summary

Starting with Drupal 12 (main), the tests directory under Drupal core is excluded from the packages that most sites actually download: the Composer "dist" zip and the release tarballs built by drupal.org. This shrinks the on-disk footprint of a typical Drupal installation (tests accounted for a large share of core's total file count) and removes test code, which the issue's participants noted has occasionally been a source of security concerns, from production deployments. Nothing changes for anyone working from a git checkout of core, including core contributors and the testbot. Sites and projects that need to run tests which rely on core's test base classes or core-only test modules (for example when testing custom or contributed code against core, or applying patches that touch test files) need to install drupal/core from source instead of from the default dist package.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: Projects that run automated tests extending core test base classes (e.g. KernelTestBase, WebDriverTestBase) or depending on core test-only modules must install drupal/core from source (e.g. composer install --prefer-source for that package) since dist packages/tarballs no longer ship core/tests.

Technical details

The mechanism is a new core/.gitattributes file with a tests export-ignore (and .gitattributes export-ignore) directive. Drupal.org's packaging pipeline builds releases with git-archive, which honors export-ignore, so the entire core/tests directory is dropped from both the packaged tarball and the Composer dist zip without any change to the packaging scripts themselves.

This landed in three steps. The first commit (5341dd83) tried a fine-grained approach, excluding most test paths but carving out exceptions such as modules/*/tests/src/ and profiles/tests/testing/ so that base test classes contrib relies on (like WebDriverTestBase) would survive in dist packages. That broke contrib CI within hours because those base classes still depend on test-only helper modules (js_testing_ajax_request_test, js_testing_log_test, css_disable_transitions_test, entity_test, performance_test, etc.) that lived in the excluded paths, so it was reverted (34b130bd). After discussion of the maintenance burden of an ever-growing exceptions list versus the simplicity of --prefer-source, the maintainers landed a much simpler final version (b8367add): core/.gitattributes excludes the entire tests directory, with no carve-outs, on the understanding that anyone needing core's test infrastructure installs drupal/core from source.

Because Package Manager's own build tests assemble a Composer project from the checked-out core codebase, its TemplateProjectTestBase::createTestProject() now explicitly mirrors the package_manager module's own test modules into the built test project, since those modules are no longer present when core is installed as a dist package.

Follow-up work was split out rather than handled here: a gitlab_templates change to default CI to --prefer-source for drupal/core, plus separate issues #3625050 (documenting composer-patches usage without patching tests) and #3625358 (deciding what to do with run-tests.sh and similar dev scripts in dist builds, which currently fail without the excluded test code).</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">If your project or CI pipeline runs tests that depend on Drupal core's test base classes, traits, or test-only modules (for example Drupal\Tests\...\KernelTestBase, WebDriverTestBase, or fixture/test modules under core/tests or core/modules/*/tests), install drupal/core from source rather than from dist, for instance:

composer install --prefer-source

or, to target only core:

composer config --global preferred-install.drupal/core source

Patches that modify files under any tests directory will also fail to apply against a dist install of core; see #3625050 for guidance on stripping test-only changes from patches.

item.title: #3532930: Make Drupal\Core\Database\Database type strict and PHPStan L10 compliant
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +271/−173 · php +271/−173
  • Diff: 3a8ca18

  • Followers: 11

Summary

The Drupal\Core\Database\Database class, along with Connection::setKey()/setTarget() and Log::__construct(), has been made type strict and fully documented for PHPStan's strictest level. Connection keys and targets (the identifiers used to select which database to talk to, e.g. 'default') have always been documented as strings, but the code silently accepted integers too. That silent acceptance is now deprecated: passing an integer key or target still works today but triggers a deprecation notice and will throw a TypeError once removed in Drupal 13. Sites and contributed modules that pass integers as database keys or targets (for example in multi-database setups) should switch to strings.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Drupal\Core\Database\Database's static methods now declare native string|int parameter types and return types (e.g. getConnection(string|int $target = 'default', string|int|null $key = NULL): Connection) instead of being untyped, and the class itself now uses declare(strict_types=1).
  • Deprecation: Passing a non-string value as the database connection $key or $target to Drupal\Core\Database\Database methods (getConnection(), addConnectionInfo(), startLog(), getLog(), setActiveConnection(), getConnectionInfo(), renameConnection(), removeConnection(), openConnection(), closeConnection(), ignoreTarget(), getConnectionInfoAsUrl()), to Connection::setKey()/setTarget(), or to Log::__construct() is deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and is removed from drupal:13.0.0.

Technical details

The class gained declare(strict_types=1); and PHPStan-level-10-compliant documentation, including new @phpstan-type array shapes (UnprocessedConnectionInfoArray, ConnectionInfoArray in Database.php, DatabaseLogEntry in Log.php) that describe the connection-info and query-log array structures instead of relying on array alone. All previously-untyped static methods (startLog(), getLog(), getConnection(), setActiveConnection(), parseConnectionInfo(), addConnectionInfo(), getConnectionInfo(), getAllConnectionInfo(), setMultipleConnectionInfo(), renameConnection(), removeConnection(), openConnection(), closeConnection(), ignoreTarget(), getConnectionInfoAsUrl()) now declare native parameter and return types, mostly string|int for keys/targets to preserve backward compatibility, with a @trigger_error() deprecation added wherever an int is passed instead of the documented string. Internally, values are cast with (string) before being handed to Connection::setTarget()/setKey() or Log's constructor, since those now also deprecate non-string input under the stricter typing PHPStan otherwise enforces across the call chain.

parseConnectionInfo() was reworked to build a fresh $connection_info array (asserting namespace/autoload end up set) rather than mutating the incoming $info in place, which also let outdated Drupal 8 backward-compatibility test cases for the old Drupal\Driver\Database\* namespace layout (removed back in #3294695) be dropped from SettingsTest. A follow-up, #3533038, proposes replacing the long connection-info array shape with a ConnectionParameters value object, but was postponed in favor of this narrower type-strictness pass. Contrib database drivers were checked for impact; the MS SQL Server driver's queue got a dedicated follow-up (#3577786) and the Oracle and DruDbal drivers were found unaffected or no longer maintained.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">Replace integer database connection keys or targets with strings wherever Drupal\Core\Database\Database methods are called, for example:

// Before (still works, but now deprecated):
Database::addConnectionInfo(100, 300, $connection_info);
Database::getConnection(200, 100);

// After:
Database::addConnectionInfo('100', '300', $connection_info);
Database::getConnection('200', '100');

The same applies to Drupal\Core\Database\Connection::setKey()/setTarget() and to the $key argument of Drupal\Core\Database\Log::__construct(). Non-string values will raise a TypeError once support is removed in Drupal 13.0.0.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: June 28, 2025
  • Committed: September 1, 2026 (1 year later)

Key contributors

  • mondrake
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • mradcliffe (Kosada)
  • dcam

Collaboration

The change nearly broke real-world usage: alexpott tested the MR and found he could currently call Database::getConnection(1) with an integer key, something that "works just fine" today, but bootstrapping failed with a TypeError once the MR's strict types were applied. That prompted mondrake and alexpott to work out, in comments #19 to #22, a softer approach: keep string|int as the accepted type but add @trigger_error() deprecation notices for integer input rather than breaking it outright, deferring the hard break to Drupal 13. mondrake also raised, in #4, that @final on an abstract class looks contradictory; the discussion concluded the class is effectively meant to be static-only and uninstantiable, but changing that further was deferred to a separate issue to avoid delaying this one.

Summary

Fifty eight unused SVG icon files have been removed from core/misc/icons. Thirty of them were only used by the Toolbar module and were copied into that module in the related issue #3622941; the other twenty eight had no references left anywhere in core. This is a main branch only (next major version) change: nothing in Drupal core itself changes behavior, but if a custom or contributed theme referenced any of these specific icon files directly (for example via background-image: url(...) pointing at core/misc/icons/...), that reference will break once sites are on the version built from this branch. Impact

The core icon set in core/misc/icons/<color>/<name>.svg is consumed by core's PostCSS build (postcss-url, configured in core/scripts/css/compile.js) which inlines referenced SVGs into compiled CSS such as the various *.icon.theme.pcss.css files. The removed files had no remaining url(...) references in any .pcss.css or .css file in core after the Toolbar module took its own copies of the 30 icons it needs (per #3622941). The commit is a pure deletion, no CSS or PHP changes; it only removes the 58 now dead SVG assets.

If a custom or contributed theme or module references any of the deleted paths directly, for example:

background-image: url(../../misc/icons/787878/wrench.svg);

copy the needed SVG into your own module/theme before upgrading, since it will no longer exist under core/misc/icons on this branch.
